newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts upbeat if underwhelmed by H1 BASF.
newsitem.headline: Analysts upbeat if underwhelmed by H1 BASF.

text.p: Analysts said on Thursday that interim figures at German chemical giant BASF AG were barely in line with expectations, prompting a slide in BASF shares which dragged other chemical stocks down with them.
BASF AG saw net income rise 3.4 percent to 1.417 billion marks in the first half of the year.

"These figures are a little bit below our expectations. There is some weakness in plastics, where the group saw price competition," Michael Stone, chemicals analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Equity Research in London.
Income in the plastics and fibres division fell to 260 million marks from 457 million in the first six months.
BASF shares were down 3.20 marks at 69 marks mid-bourse, while Hoechst fell five percent at one point. The overall market was down one percent at 4,232.83 points.

Christine Dienhart, chemicals analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank in Munich, said: "The figures were exactly in line, certainly the pre-tax figures, although there was a discrepancy in the after-tax figure in that they paid more tax than we expected.
"This could have something to do with the increased contribution from its oil and gas business, which tends to be tax-heavy," Dienhart said.

A tax rate of around 40 percent is anticipated for the full-year. Analysts said the increased tax charge was mostly related to the increased contribution of BASF's oil and gas businees, which tends to be tax-heavy.

Price pressures also came to bear in other areas of activity. "There were price pressures on some products in the health and nutrition sector, as well as higher costs for launching pharmaceutical products," said Stone.
Income was also lower in health and nutrition at 678 million marks, compared to 718 million marks in the same period last year.
BASF reported a 5.8 percent rise in pretax profit to 2.458 billion marks from 2.323 billion, a figure that came in at the lower end of what analysts had forecast.
A poll by analysts before the results had foreseen pre-tax profit of between 2.46-2.53 billion marks, up 5.9 to nine percent, and sales growth of 13.3-14.6 percent to 27.5-27.8 billion marks.
The group saw first half net income rise 3.4 percent to 1.417 billion marks, while sales grew by 14.5 percent to 27.8 billion marks from 24.3 billion.
One feature of the results released by the chemicals companies so far has been the major contribution of the strength of the dollar against the mark.

As major exporters, chemical companies benefit from this and BASF is no exception. "We can see that (dollar/mark) currency conversions boosted sales nine percent, but the group still posted good gains from volume growth," Dienhart said.
The figures were "great", he added, but not so great that they could meet the high expectations of the market.
The group said its objective of increasing earnings in 1997 and achieving group sales of more than 50 billion marks was within reach.
Stone said: "The group seems reasonably confident that it will report higher earnings for the full year, so I don't see any major collapse in the second half."

"I can see oil and gas and colorants continuing reasonably strong in the second half. There will be more pressure on the plastics sector, but health and nutrition will see the benefits of new products in the U.S.."
